title_en: Homily on the Presentation of Our Lord Jesus Christ
author: Hesychius of Jerusalem
occasion: A festal homily for the feast of the Hypapante, the Presentation of Christ in the Temple, celebrating the purification rites and the encounter with Simeon and Anna.
argument: Hesychius presents the feast of the Presentation as the feast of feasts, recapitulating the whole mystery of Christ's incarnation. He argues that Christ, though above the Law as its giver, submitted to the Law's purification rites for our sake, not because Mary or the child needed cleansing. Simeon is portrayed as a righteous man whose name means 'hearing of God,' a vehicle of the Lord and throne of God, whose righteousness possesses priesthood under its feet. His reception of the infant Christ reveals the salvation prepared for all peoples. The homily closes by interpreting the 'sign of contradiction' as the cross, which causes the fall of the faithless and the rising of those who turn to faith.

outline.move: The feast is exalted as the feast of feasts, and the Gospel account from Luke is introduced, showing Christ submitting to the Law for our sake.
Hesychius explains why Mary and the child did not need purification, and how Christ fulfilled the Law beyond the Law, with Luke's account reflecting Christ's voluntary poverty.
Simeon is introduced as righteous and devout, receives the child, and proclaims the Nunc Dimittis, recognizing the salvation prepared for all peoples.
The homily interprets the 'sign of contradiction' as the cross, discusses the fall and rising of many, and closes with a doxology.

cast.name: Hesychius
cast.who: Presbyter of Jerusalem and preacher of the homily.

cast.name: Jesus Christ
cast.who: The incarnate Lord, presented in the Temple as an infant.

cast.name: Mary
cast.who: The virgin mother of Jesus, who needed no purification.

cast.name: Joseph
cast.who: The guardian of Jesus, not his father and not subject to purification.

cast.name: Simeon
cast.who: The righteous and devout man in Jerusalem who received the infant Christ.

cast.name: Anna
cast.who: Mentioned with Simeon as receiving the offering of turtledoves, but not mentioned again in the extant text and plays no further role in the homily.

cast.name: Luke
cast.who: The evangelist whose account of the Presentation is expounded.

cast.name: Peter
cast.who: The apostle who fell but rose again and became a guide for others.

cast.name: Judas
cast.who: The betrayer who fell and hanged himself.

cast.name: Herod
cast.who: The king warned not to fear for his kingdom.

cast.name: Annas
cast.who: The high priest warned not to fear for his priesthood.

cast.name: Caiaphas
cast.who: The high priest warned not to fear for his priesthood.

cast.name: Cleopas
cast.who: One of the disciples on the road to Emmaus who spoke of Jesus as a prophet.

voices.speaker: Luke (quoted Gospel)
voices.how_marked: Introduced by phrases such as 'Οὕτω τοίνυν ἡμῖν τῆς ἑορτῆς ὁ Λουκᾶς τὴν ἱστορίαν ἐξέθετο' and quotation from the Gospel.

voices.speaker: Simeon (quoted)
voices.how_marked: Introduced by 'Καὶ βαστάζων τὸ βρέφος ἔφη' and direct quotation of the Nunc Dimittis.

voices.speaker: Ezekiel (quoted prophet)
voices.how_marked: Introduced by 'παρὰ τοῦ Ἰεζεκιὴλ μάνθανε' and direct quotation.

voices.speaker: Zephaniah (quoted prophet)
voices.how_marked: Introduced by 'Σοφονίας ὁ προφήτης τὸν θεὸν αὐτὸν εἰσήγαγε λέγοντα' and direct quotation.

voices.speaker: Peter (quoted retrospectively)
voices.how_marked: The quotations 'Τὴν ψυχήν μου ὑπὲρ σοῦ θήσω' and 'Ἐὰν δέῃ με σὺν σοὶ ἀποθανεῖν, οὐ μή σε ἀπαρνήσομαι' are attributed to him retrospectively. The 'ὁ μὲν... ὁ δέ' construction contrasts Judas and Peter, but Peter's words are introduced indirectly.

voices.speaker: Judas (quoted)
voices.how_marked: Introduced by 'ὁ μὲν ὡς εἰπών' with the quotation 'Τί μοι θέλετε δοῦναι, κἀγὼ ὑμῖν παραδώσω αὐτόν;' This is the only quotation from Judas, and the contrast is with Peter's fall and restoration.

voices.speaker: The crowd, the elders and scribes, and the centurion (quoted)
voices.how_marked: The crowd is introduced by 'Ὁ λαὸς ἐβόα' with 'Σταύρωσον αὐτόν'; the elders and scribes are quoted with 'Ἐμνήσθημεν ὅτι ὁ πλάνος ἐκεῖνος εἶπεν...'; the centurion is introduced by 'Ὁ δὲ ἑκατόνταρχος ἐβόα' with 'Ἀληθῶς θεοῦ υἱὸς ἦν οὗτος.'

voices.speaker: Cleopas and companion (quoted)
voices.how_marked: Introduced by 'τοὺς περὶ Κλεόπαν μαθητὰς παριόντας καὶ πρὸς αὐτὸν λέγειν'. The quotation is in two parts: first a statement, then a response to a question ('ἐρωτηθέντες'). The dialogue structure includes an interlocutor.

key_terms.sense: The feast of the Presentation, the meeting of the infant Christ with Simeon and Anna in the Temple.
The purification rites prescribed by the Law of Moses after childbirth.
Christ as the giver of the Law, who nevertheless submits to the Law.
The virginity of Mary, preserved intact in childbirth.
Mary as the one who bore God in the flesh.
The consolation of Israel that Simeon awaited, fulfilled in Christ.
The salvation prepared by God, seen by Simeon in the infant Christ.
The sign of contradiction, interpreted as the cross, which causes division and reveals hearts.
The fall of those who persist in unbelief, contrasted with the rising of those who turn to faith.
The rising of those who turn from unbelief to faith, and ultimately the resurrection.
The sword that pierces Mary's soul, interpreted as division and doubt.
The cross of Christ, the sign of contradiction and the source of peace.

scripture: The author quotes from the Septuagint and the Gospel of Luke. Psalm numbering follows the Septuagint. Citations should be given in modern form, e.g., Luke 2:22-24, Ezekiel 44:1-2, Zephaniah 1:12.
uncertain: The exact date of the homily is not stated in the text.
The precise occasion beyond the feast of the Presentation is not specified.
Whether the homily was delivered in Jerusalem or elsewhere is not indicated.

_unresolved_facts.claim: Simeon is portrayed as a righteous man whose name means 'hearing of God,' a vehicle of the Lord and throne of God, whose righteousness possesses priesthood under its feet.
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: ὄχημα ὑπῆρχε δεσποτικὸν ὁ Συμεών, θρόνος θεοῦ... ἡ δικαιοσύνη δὲ τὴν ἱερωσύνην ὑπὸ τοὺς πόδας κέκτηται
_unresolved_facts.fix: Simeon is called 'a vehicle of the Lord' (ὄχημα δεσποτικὸν) and 'throne of God' (θρόνος θεοῦ), and it is stated that 'righteousness possesses priesthood under its feet' (ἡ δικαιοσύνη δὲ τὴν ἱερωσύνην ὑπὸ τοὺς πόδας κέκτηται)—a general statement, not specifically that Simeon's righteousness possesses priesthood under its feet.

_unresolved_facts.claim: Anna... plays no further role in the homily
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: ζεῦγος τρυγόνων λογικῶν τῷ Συμεὼν καὶ τῇ Ἅννᾳ προσέφερεν
_unresolved_facts.fix: Anna is mentioned once in the opening as receiving the offering of turtledoves with Simeon, but does not appear again in the extant text.

_unresolved_facts.claim: Peter (quoted retrospectively)... The 'ὁ μὲν... ὁ δέ' construction contrasts Judas and Peter, but Peter's words are introduced indirectly.
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: ὁ μὲν ὡς εἰπών· «Τί μοι θέλετε δοῦναι, κἀγὼ ὑμῖν παραδώσω αὐτόν;» ὁ δὲ ὡς εἰπών· «Τὴν ψυχήν μου ὑπὲρ σοῦ θήσω»... «Ἐὰν δέῃ με σὺν σοὶ ἀποθανεῖν, οὐ μή σε ἀπαρνήσομαι.»
_unresolved_facts.fix: Both Peter and Judas are introduced with identical constructions: 'ὁ μὲν ὡς εἰπών' and 'ὁ δὲ ὡς εἰπών'. Peter's words are quoted directly just as Judas's are, not 'indirectly' or 'retrospectively' in any different manner.

_unresolved_facts.claim: The dialogue structure includes an interlocutor.
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: ὥστε τοὺς περὶ Κλεόπαν μαθητὰς παριόντας καὶ πρὸς αὐτὸν λέγειν· «Σὺ μόνος παροικεῖς ἐν Ἰερουσαλὴμ καὶ οὐκ ἔγνως τὰ γενόμενα ἐν αὐτῇ ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις ταύταις.» Εἶτα ἐρωτηθέντες «ποῖα;» ἐπήγαγον· «Τὰ περὶ Ἰησοῦ τοῦ Ναζωραίου, ὃς ἐγένετο ἀνὴρ προφήτης, καὶ τὰ ἑξῆς.»
_unresolved_facts.fix: The Cleopas quotation involves a question 'ποῖα;' asked by an unnamed interlocutor, but this is part of the narrative description, not a separate voice marked as a speaker in the homily.

_unresolved_facts.claim: Cleopas... One of the disciples on the road to Emmaus who spoke of Jesus as a prophet.
_unresolved_facts.fix: Cleopas is mentioned as the one around whom the disciples are grouped ('οἱ περὶ Κλεόπαν'), not as a single disciple speaking alone. The plural 'μαθητὰς' and 'ἐπήγαγον' indicate multiple disciples speaking.
